topics.label: Lecture framing: cancer hallmarks and their genetic basis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes the lecture’s aims, its relationship to earlier lectures, and the hallmark framework used throughout.

topics.label: Signaling mutations that deregulate growth and survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signaling pathways free cancer cells from normal controls on proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Disrupted differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how altered differentiation produces malignant cell populations and disrupts normal tissue renewal.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how disruption of the p53–Bax–BCL2 balance allows cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and replicative immortalization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells overcome telomere-dependent limits on division by restoring telomerase expression.

topics.label: p53-mediated genome protection and growth-control recap
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain p53’s protective responses to cellular stress and conclude the discussion of genetically disrupted growth control.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered metabolism supports cancer and interacts with the genetic and epigenetic changes driving it.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how the angiogenic switch supplies developing tumors with the perfusion needed for continued growth.

topics.label: Metastatic spread and successful colonization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how tumor cells reach distant sites and what determines whether they establish clinically detectable metastases.

topics.label: Closing synthesis and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by restating its central message, recommending further reading, and inviting questions before the practicals.
